verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The Lean states the same Leibniz rule in general form, for an arbitrary scalar f on Euclidean three-space: curl(f·B) = ∇f × B + f curl B, with `SpatialCurl.curl` the genuine Euclidean curl (curlLinear of the Fréchet derivative, SpatialCurl.lean:30-48) and `cross` the standard right-handed cross product (cross_zero/one/two give u₁v₂-u₂v₁ etc.), so signs and orientation agree. The recovery is one substitution plus one chain rule: put f(y) = χ(a q(t,y)) and B = A_j; then ∇f = a χ'(aq) ∇q by `scaledCutoff_iteratedDeriv` at n = 1 together with the composite derivative step already carried out at GenericSolenoidalRealization.lean:81, which gives exactly the paper's second term a χ'(aq) ∇q × A_j. The only other discrepancy is the order of the two summands. The combined instance is not written as its own declaration.
